subject: Dedicated GPU sizing and SLA / burst alignment for Orion Tech RFP
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@oriontech.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@oriontech.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:15:00 -0800
Subject: RFP Q: Dedicated GPU sizing + burst/SLA alignment

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for agreeing to look at our sizing questions. We're finalizing an RFP and need a compact response about how Redwood would size dedicated capacity (reserved + burst) for our production workloads. High level:
- 24/7 chat endpoint for a large internal assistant: average concurrent active requests ~75, peak 250 (peaks last 5-15 minutes)
- Model family: mix of open families (Llama2-70B and a trimmed 13B variant) for chat; embeddings use a small 2B encoder model
- Expected tokens/day: 6.5M tokens generation + 1.2M tokens embedding calls
- P95 latency target for interactive chat: <=200ms (token streaming ok)
- Cost sensitivity: want to balance reserved commit vs burst; procurement wants guidance on commit ramp (3/6/12 months)

Can you confirm recommended GPU types, a suggested reserved pool vs burst pool, and any latency/throughput SLAs we should expect? I've attached the RFP workbook with a workload profile and sample traces.

Thanks,
Elaine
Procurement | Orion Tech
attachment: orion_rfp_workbook_v3.xlsx (xlsx)
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@oriontech.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP Q: Dedicated GPU sizing + burst/SLA alignment

Hi Elaine — thanks for the workbook, got it. A few quick clarifying questions before we run a detailed sizing:
1) Are the concurrency numbers measured as active model token-producing streams or incoming HTTP requests (some requests fan out to multiple model calls)?
2) For peak windows (250 concurrent), how long do peaks typically last? You mentioned 5-15 min — can you confirm 90% of peaks are < 20 min?
3) Is cross-region failover required (we can reserve in primary region + warm-failover pool in a second region)?

If you can confirm, we'll run a mixed-workload simulation and send a recommended GPU mix and reservation ramp. For initial ballpark: given your latency target and model families, H100-class (80GB) for the 70B instances + A100 40GB for 13B inference is likely the optimal mix; embeddings can run on cheaper A10/T4 equivalence depending on throughput. But we'll validate.

- Aditya
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Park <elaine@oriontech.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@oriontech.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP Q: Dedicated GPU sizing + burst/SLA alignment

Hi Aditya — quick answers:
1) Concurrency = active token-streaming sessions (one HTTP session = one active stream). No multi-call fan-out for the chat flow.
2) Peak windows are typically 8-12 minutes; 95th percentile peaks < 25 min.
3) Cross-region failover is required for business continuity; primary is us-west, secondary is us-east.

We'll expect a recommended reserved pool in us-west and a warm-failover or smaller reserved pool in us-east. Please include cost delta for burst-only traffic vs reserved units.

Elaine
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@oriontech.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood sizing recommendation for Orion Tech (initial)

Hi Elaine / Aditya,

Attached is our initial sizing workbook (redwood_sizing_recommendation_v1.xlsx) and a summarized recommendation below. We ran a cost/throughput simulation using the workload traces in your workbook and a mixed-model profile (70B L2 family tuned, + 13B trimmed variant, embeddings workload). Key assumptions: average generation tokens per request = 85, average generation length per session = 12 tokens/sec for streaming; peak concurrency 250 for bursts; reserved pool target to hit 95% of baseline traffic without burst.

Summary recommendation (US-WEST primary):
- Reserved pool (commit): 8 x H100-80GB (for 70B family, lowest p95 latency) + 10 x A100-40GB (for 13B trimmed and mixed-density serving)
  - Expected steady-state coverage: ~78% of average daily traffic; p95 latency target ~120ms on H100, ~150ms on A100 for 13B.
- Burst pool (shared, autoscale): additional 6 x A100-40GB and 4 x A10-class nodes for embeddings spikes
  - Burst policy: auto-scale up during 5-25 minute peaks, pre-warm GPUs using predictive warm-up when traffic trend indicates approaching peak (based on your traces)
- Warm-failover (US-EAST): 4 x H100-80GB + 6 x A100-40GB reserved at lower commit (can be kept on standby to meet cross-region RTO)
- Quantization & model variant strategy: 4-bit quantized 13B variant for non-critical paths (saves ~35% compute), keep unquantized 70B on H100 for highest quality where latency-critical.

Throughput & latency projections (from simulation):
- Average tokens/sec served (cluster-wide, during business hours): ~4,200 tokens/sec
- Peak tokens/sec during 250 concurrent sessions: ~13,500 tokens/sec (handled by reserved + burst pool)
- P95 token latency: 120ms (70B on H100, reserved capacity), 150-180ms for 13B on A100 under mixed load with burst included

Cost & commit guidance:
- 3-month ramp: start with 50% of recommended reserved pool (4 H100 + 5 A100) + configured burst pool; useful to validate traffic pattern and warm-up policies.
- 6-month: increase to 75% reserved if observed peak load matches projections.
- 12-month: full commit for cost optimization and predictable throughput.
- We estimate a 22-28% uplift in unit cost if you rely on burst-only for peak coverage vs committing to the recommended reserved pool (details in workbook).

Attachments: redwood_sizing_recommendation_v1.xlsx (contains per-model throughput matrix, kernel-fits, sample job packing, and cost delta table).

Next steps we propose:
1) Internal validation call to walk your infra/procurement team through the workbook (30-45 min)
2) Trial reservation: 4 H100 + 6 A100 reserved for 30 days with burst policy enabled to validate warm-up and autoscaling behavior
3) Add a follow-up procurement SOW sketch with commit tiers and SLA language for p95 latency and availability

Happy to join procurement call next week.

- Monica
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
attachment: redwood_sizing_recommendation_v1.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@oriontech.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood sizing recommendation for Orion Tech (initial)

Thanks Monica — this looks like a sensible starting point. A couple of implementation notes for procurement and SRE to consider:
1) SLA / Fallback: include explicit fallback policy in SOW — when reserved capacity is saturated, traffic should failover to the burst pool using a policy that prioritizes sessions by token-length and customer-critical flags. We can provide a Canary fallback policy for the first 30 days.
2) Quantization options: we can offer an additional reserved lane for 4-bit quantized 13B instances which gives ~30-40% cost savings and can be deployed under a lower-latency SLO if Orion is willing to accept occasional small quality deltas.
3) Pre-warm hooks: we'll expose a warm-up API so your front-end can trigger pre-warm loads based on anticipated prompts (we recommend 90s lead time for H100s on cold-starts).

Monica — can you add a short fallback ladder and canary rollout step into the workbook and send an updated cost delta? Elaine — if these options are acceptable, we'll draft the 30-day pilot reservation SOW and a sample SLA clause for review.

- Vivek
Director, Product Solutions | Redwood Inference
